title: Quenched Silky Malaysian Millet Pilaf
description: A comforting and lacto-vegetarian-friendly Malaysian dish featuring millet, with a silky texture and fermented flavors, served on a hot-stone-plate.
instructions: Rinse the millet in a fine mesh sieve and drain well.
In a medium saucepan, combine the millet and water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until the millet is tender and the water is absorbed.
In a large skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until it is lightly browned and caramelized.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the skillet and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in the fermented soybean paste and cook for 1 minute.
Fluff the cooked millet with a fork and stir in the coconut milk, salt, and cooked onion mixture.
Arrange the sashimi-cut portobello mushrooms on top of the millet pilaf.
Serve the quenched silky Malaysian millet pilaf on a hot-stone-plate immediately.
